en: I bow to the beautiful Gopāla, who wears a forest garland, whose eyes are wide, and who removes all suffering;
the moon of Vṛndāvana, the root of bliss, supreme joy, and the upholder of the earth.

Worship the son of Nanda, who is as dark as a beloved rain-cloud, whose desires are fulfilled, who is exceedingly charming, who bestows joy, who is the essence of all happiness, the contemplation of reality, and the supreme Brahman. 1.
With a face like a beautiful lotus, having conquered Māra, the abode of bliss, wearing a crown,
with a necklace of *guñjā* berries, sporting in the forest, supremely noble, and clad in bark garments.
Clad in the yellow garment of his beloved, having made his sacred thread of his own hand, he is the most excellent among the wise.
The bank of the Yamunā is most exceedingly blissful, its dust beautifying the face [of Kṛṣṇa] and its trees providing incomparable shade;
it is graced by the dust of His face, where cows roam, and where the flute is played with sweet sound.
It is dear to Him, possessing most pure auspicious lotus feet and stainless luster from His nails, which dispels the darkness [of ignorance]. (3)
He whose head and crown are beautiful, whose hair is curled, who possesses the attire of a preeminent dancer, and who is the bestower of desires;
he who is a human being created by Māyā, the younger brother of Haladhara (Balarāma), the destroyer of demons, and the bearer of the world's burden;
the protector of his beloved Vraja, who moves with graceful charm, who is ever-beneficial at all times, and the most excellent of all states of being. 4.
He who has the luster of a blue lotus, who manifests the assembly of gods, who is the blossoming of flowers, and who holds the flute;
he who has subdued the god of love within his heart, a treasury of beauty, who performs sweet songs and captivates the mind;
he whose beloved smiles softly, who dwells in the forest groves, who possesses manifold charms, and who engages in divine play. || 5 ||
Exceedingly skillful, protecting the distressed, dependent on his devotees, a servant of action;
enchanting, most steadfast, a hero with the strength of serpents, having slain enemy heroes, most restless;
the delighter of the beloved cowherd community, lotus-faced, the subduer of Balarāma, and the bearer of the mountain. 6.

His body possesses the luster of a rain-cloud; he is gracefully curved in three places (the *tribhaṅga* pose); he has performed many waves of sport; he is the best among connoisseurs of aesthetic flavor (*rasika*).
He is surrounded by the circle of Gokula; his form is like that of the God of Love; he sports in the forest groves; he is most profound.
He is the moon to his beloved Vraja; he is of auspicious and beautiful will; he has bestowed bliss; he removes all delusion. (7)
I bow to Him whose pair of feet are worshipped, who purifies all, who uplifts the world, and whose nature is stainless;
who went to the head of the serpent Kāliya, who caused the hooded snakes to bow, and who destroyed the power of Yama;
who removes the suffering of His beloved, whose feet are pure, who is the refuge of the helpless, and the bestower of liberation. (8)
Thus ends the Śrī Nandakumāra-aṣṭaka composed by the venerable Mahāprabhu Vallabhācārya.
